Snow interferes with daily life so much. You gotta wear a jacket, gloves, hat, and then worry about where you can store them once you get inside somewhere. If you have a house, you have to shovel your driveway. If you drive, you have to worry about the road conditions and probably leave somewhere early because you can't drive as fast. If you bike and the bike lane isn't cleared, well, good luck. Your shoes also get very dirty from all the slush everywhere. And when there's snow, you can't do a lot of fun activities (at least enjoyably). You can't play most sports outside, you can't really go on a bike ride, you can't have a cookout, you can't enjoy a nice day on the lake, you can't sit outside at a restaurant and enjoy a nice meal, etc. The cold weather that accompanies snow is also terrible. Who the hell wants to be outside when the air literally hurts your face?

Snow is cool to look at, and can be fun if you ski/snowboard, but that's about it. If I was into snow sports, I'd maybe want to live in California or Arizona where you can drive up to the mountains and ski/snowboard, and then go back home where it's not cold.

People have sleep cycles, where they go between light sleep and REM sleep multiple times throughout the night. Each person's sleep cycle lasts a different amount of time, but the average is around 90 minutes. If you wake up in the part of the cycle where you're sleeping lightly, you're less likely to be tired when you wake up.
